key_insight: A self-supervised, generalized safety measure learned from large-scale naturalistic driving data can predict collision risk (crashes and near-crashes) in real time without manual labels, providing earlier and reliable warnings for timely reactions.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of scalable, label-free methods to estimate imminent collision risk from everyday driving data and deliver early, actionable warnings for autonomous systems.
method: Train a risk model on vast naturalistic driving logs using self-supervised objectives that identify temporal precursors of crashes and near-crashes without manual labels.
Learn a generalized safety representation that transfers across scenarios and runs in real time to produce an early-warning risk score.
Validate the measure at scale against real crashes/near-crashes to demonstrate improved warning lead time and reliable detection compared to baselines.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable approach for runtime safety monitoring and evaluation of autonomous systems that reduces reliance on rare labeled crash data and enables earlier interventions to prevent collisions.
visual_elements: Timeline plot showing risk score rising before a crash/near-crash (lead time annotated)
Schematic: training pipeline from large-scale unlabeled driving logs to self-supervised risk model
Performance chart (e.g., detection rate vs. lead time or ROC/PR curves) comparing the proposed risk measure to baselines
Dashboard mockup or vehicle HUD icon set illustrating real-time warning integration and action window
paper_title: Learning collision risk proactively from naturalistic driving data at scale
paper_authors: Yiru Jiao, Simeon C. Calvert, Sander van Cranenburgh, Hans van Lint
